design_detail: Corrigendum (a correction notice, not a study) to Kvam et al. (2025), 'MDMA-assisted therapy as a treatment for major depressive disorder: proof of principle study', Br J Psychiatry 227:783–789. Published in Br J Psychiatry 228(4):388 (online 10 February 2026; print issue April 2026 per Crossref), open access (CC BY-SA). One paragraph of explanation and a corrected Table 2. Read in PubMed Central (PMC13051208) in the app's browser, with the original article (PMC12550655) and both Crossref records. Card design 'narrative-review' is the schema's closest category for an editorial notice, as for the retraction notes on this page. Reference id assigned by this reader ('a' because the same first author has another 2026 paper on the evidence map, the seven-month follow-up, assigned 'b').
can_establish: That the authors corrected one participant's post-treatment MADRS score in Table 2 and in the Primary outcome section of the 2025 article, that the corrected outcome mean is 10.3 (SD 8.3), and that they state the responder and remitter counts, the scores of the nine participants without PTSD, the interpretation and the conclusions are unchanged.
cannot_establish: What the error was, whose score it was or how the corrected value was obtained; why the mean change, its interval and the test statistic were unaffected; or whether the other rows of Table 2 that do not add up are right.

analysis.effect_sizes: Corrected MADRS row: baseline 29.6 (SD 4.9), outcome 10.3 (8.3), difference −19.3 (95% CI −14.9 to −23.7), z = −3.06, P < 0.001; all other rows of Table 2 reprinted unchanged.
analysis.selective_reporting: The notice gives no corrected SD of the change (the original Results gave 8.3, the value now printed as the outcome SD) and does not mention the abstract.

interpretation_gap.results_show: One participant's post-treatment MADRS score was wrong in the published article; correcting it changes the outcome mean from 9.7 (SD 10.0) to 10.3 (8.3), which now matches the printed change of −19.3 from a baseline of 29.6.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The notice calls it a minor error, discovered on analysing follow-up data, that does not affect the responder or remitter counts, the scores of the nine participants without comorbid PTSD, the interpretation or the conclusions.

timeline.event: Kvam et al., Br J Psychiatry: the corrected article (online 11 July 2025; card sc_kvam_2025).

replication.where_it_stands: Read with the article it corrects; the corrected values are used on card sc_kvam_2025. The PMC copy of the article itself still shows the uncorrected figure, with a link to this notice.

funding.declared_conflicts: None stated in the notice; the article's declarations apply.
funding.affiliations_note: Same eleven authors as the article (Crossref record and PMC page).

what_would_settle_it: Publication of the participant-level MADRS data, or a corrected table in which every row's difference agrees with its baseline and outcome means.

domains.note: Not a review: the notice corrects the authors' own article, so nothing is selected.
The notice does not say what the error was or how it was found, beyond its discovery during analysis of follow-up data.

domains.domain: Reliance on the authors' own studies
domains.note: Concerns only the authors' own article, by its nature.
States the correction and its consequences without speculation.

domains.domain: Balance of the correction's scope (what is corrected and what is left)
domains.note: Three other rows of Table 2 whose differences do not equal baseline minus outcome (GAD-7 and two SDS items) are reprinted unchanged and not discussed.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: No validated instrument applies to correction notices; the editors' narrative-review checklist is used as the closest, its domains read as questions about the notice. The notice is the primary record of the correction and may be cited for the corrected MADRS outcome mean and for the authors' statement that the responder and remitter counts are unchanged; it does not resolve the other inconsistencies in Table 2.

key_findings.finding: The authors report a minor error in one participant's post-treatment MADRS score, discovered after analysis of follow-up data; they state it does not affect the number of responders or remitters, the MADRS scores of the nine participants without comorbid PTSD, the interpretation or the conclusions.

Corrected Table 2: MADRS (primary outcome) 29.6 (SD 4.9) at baseline and 10.3 (8.3) at outcome, difference −19.3 (95% CI −14.9 to −23.7), z = −3.06, P < 0.001; the SDS and exploratory rows are reprinted as in the article. The same corrected values apply to the article's Primary outcome section (p. 785).
key_findings.locator: Corrected Table 2 (MADRS row); corrigendum text, final paragraph

key_findings.finding: Crossref: the article's record (10.1192/bjp.2025.10320) carries an updated-by link of type correction, from the publisher, to this notice; the notice's record (vol. 228, issue 4, p. 388; online 10 February 2026, print April 2026) carries the matching update-to link.

reporting_issues.issue: The corrected table still contains rows whose printed difference is not baseline minus outcome: GAD-7 13.8 to 6.0 (−7.8, printed −9.0), SDS days lost 2.5 to 1.0 (−1.5, printed −2.0), SDS underproductive days 6.1 to 2.4 (−3.7, printed −4.1).

The notice does not give the corrected SD of the MADRS change (the article's Results gave 8.3, which is now also the printed SD of the outcome) and does not mention the abstract, whose MADRS interval (−14.8 to −23.8) differs from the table's.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML (corrigendum; article Abstract and Results › Primary outcome)

verification.source_read: PMC full text PMC13051208 (the whole notice and corrected table), read in this reader's own browser tab together with the original article PMC12550655; Crossref records of both DOIs.
